name: Asish Mohapatra
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, OfBusiness (OFB Tech), Gurugram
profile: IIT Kharagpur B.Tech and ISB MBA who worked at ITC, McKinsey and Matrix Partners India before co-founding OfBusiness in 2015, a tech platform combining raw-material procurement with credit for SMEs. OfBusiness became a SoftBank-backed unicorn; its lending arm Oxyzo is run by his wife and co-founder Ruchi Kalra.
interesting_fact: OfBusiness started by supplying steel for guardrail manufacturing; Mohapatra has said the founders faced 73 investor rejections in 2016 before the company went on to become a unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Born while his parents were researchers at IIT Kharagpur, he grew up in Cuttack, Odisha (and says he loves Cuttack's thunka puri); he traces his entrepreneurial spark to a Class 3 school essay he researched on Walt Disney.

public_contacts.value: https://www.ofbusiness.com/about/news (Press & Media page with media kit)

notes: No published press email; only a general support address (getsupport@ofbusiness.in) on the company site. Team page links his LinkedIn. Has done podcasts (e.g. KPMG Startup Speakeasy).

name: Zhao Yiwei
current_role: CEO, Hangzhou Valgen Medtech (德晋医疗), per 36Kr project page
profile: Zhao Yiwei (赵亦伟) is listed as CEO of Hangzhou Valgen Medtech, founded in 2015 in Hangzhou and focused on transcatheter mitral and tricuspid valve repair. Valgen's DragonFly transcatheter mitral clip won NMPA approval in Nov 2023 and EU MDR/CE approval in April 2025; the company raised a Series B in 2021 led by investors incl. HongShan and Qiming.
interesting_fact: Valgen's DragonFly was the first domestically developed transfemoral transcatheter mitral repair device approved in China, and the first Chinese mitral device to obtain CE certification (April 2025); the firm claims 600+ patents filed worldwide.
notes: Very little public bio info; 36Kr names Zhao Yiwei (赵亦伟) as CEO but no source found explicitly calling him founder, and legal representative is 张庭超. Company emails are general corporate contacts (Chinese-language site). 2026 strategic investment from 瑛泰医疗 reported by 36Kr.

name: Mikhail Seregine
current_role: Co-founder, Outschool (current operating role not confirmed)
profile: Former Google employee who co-founded Outschool in 2015 with CEO Amir Nathoo and ex-Airbnb engineer Nick Grandy. The Y Combinator-backed San Francisco platform offers live small-group online classes for kids; it boomed in the pandemic, reaching unicorn status in April 2021 and a $3B valuation after a $110M Tiger Global-led Series D in Oct 2021.
interesting_fact: Outschool went from first class in 2017 to a $3 billion valuation in October 2021, after pandemic school closures drove a surge in demand; Lightspeed invested at the Series B in 2020.
notes: Very low public profile: no interviews, personal site or verified social accounts found. Aggregator profiles mention Google product/engineering roles (unverified detail). No published press email found on outschool.com; route via Outschool company channels.

name: Anu Sudarsan
current_role: Manager, Engineering at Starburst (listed among the company's founders)
profile: Software engineer listed among Starburst's founders, alongside CEO Justin Borgman and the Trino co-creators. She previously worked with Starburst's founding engineers at Hadapt (acquired by Teradata in 2014). At Starburst, the Trino-based data lakehouse/query-engine company, she has led Starburst Galaxy engineering and now serves as an engineering manager.
interesting_fact: She led the projects that brought Starburst to the Google Cloud Marketplace and Azure Cloud Marketplace, and was team lead for Starburst Galaxy, its fully managed cloud offering.
deep_cut_fact: Before Starburst she worked at Hadapt (later acquired by Teradata) alongside the engineers who would later found Starburst; in 2021 she said what she liked best was getting 'to experiment with cutting-edge technologies.'
notes: Engineering-focused, low public profile; no personal social accounts verified. Starburst leadership page lists her under 'Founders' as Manager, Engineering. Older releases list Beth Winkowski (Winkowski PR) as media contact.

name: Peter Chaljawski
current_role: Founder of Berlin Brands Group (formerly Chal-Tec); stepped down as CEO in January 2024
profile: Berlin entrepreneur who founded Chal-Tec in 2005 at 19, selling affordable DJ and event gear on eBay, then expanded into audio and household appliances (Klarstein, auna, blumfeldt). Renamed Berlin Brands Group in 2019, it became a D2C/Amazon-marketplace unicorn backed by Ardian. He handed the CEO role to ex-eBay manager Eben Sermon in Jan 2024 after 18 years.
interesting_fact: He skipped university: he postponed his studies, never started them, and used his savings to found Chal-Tec, saying 'we basically democratized DJ equipment' by offering affordable alternatives to premium brands.
deep_cut_fact: The company began because at 18 he wanted DJ equipment and found only expensive premium gear or cheap junk; he asked why there was no 'Zara' of DJ gear. Its first eBay sale came in 2007, and he personally oversaw construction of the company's central warehouse.
notes: Left CEO role Jan 2024 (Börsen-Zeitung, https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/personen/berlin-brands-group-holt-ebay-veteranen-an-die-spitze). A deutsche-startups.de headline links him to 'D11Z.Ventures' investments (not verified). Named to Capital's Top 40 under 40 (2021). BBG website was unreachable this session; no contact verified.

name: Oz Alon
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, HoneyBook (San Francisco / Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded HoneyBook in 2013 with Naama Alon and Dror Shimoni after a Tel Aviv accelerator, then moved the team to Silicon Valley via a Palo Alto accelerator. HoneyBook is a clientflow, payments and AI-powered business-management platform for independent business owners; as CEO he led its 2026 expansion to the UK and Australia.
interesting_fact: HoneyBook was named to CNBC's 2026 list of the world's top fintech companies; the company has offices in San Francisco and Tel Aviv and launched in the UK and Australia in May 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech, he ran a bar called Backy on Ibn Gvirol Street in Tel Aviv and threw large all-inclusive parties with thousands of guests; he was a law-firm intern when he quit to go all in on HoneyBook, drawing on that event-organizer experience.

public_contacts.value: Dan Edelstein, InboundJunction - pr@inboundjunction.com (HoneyBook release contact)

notes: Active public speaker/podcast guest (e.g. 'From bar to unicorn' podcast). HoneyBook releases have used varying media contacts (in-house comms and agencies like BAM by BIG for UK/AU launch).

name: Lucas Hansen
current_role: Co-founder, CivAI (Civic AI Security Program); co-founder and board member, Qualia
profile: Co-founded Qualia in 2015 with Nate Baker and Joel Gottsegen; Qualia is a real-estate closing/title software platform (unicorn). In 2023 he co-founded CivAI, a Berkeley nonprofit that uses live software demos (deepfakes, phishing, AI biosecurity risks) to educate lawmakers and the public about AI capabilities and dangers.
interesting_fact: CivAI, which he co-founded in response to ChatGPT's launch, gives private AI-risk demos to lawmakers and national-security officials, and is a member of the NIST AI Safety Institute Consortium; its tools were used at the 2025 AI Action Summit.
deep_cut_fact: In October 2025 he wrote a Wall Street Journal op-ed, 'I Need a Chatbot That Won't Drive Me Crazy,' arguing AI firms should be liable for harms like chatbot-induced psychosis if they don't take adequate precautions. He met his CivAI co-founder Siddharth Hiregowdara while working together at Qualia.
notes: Now focused on AI safety (very relevant for an AI/data-center podcast angle); frequently quoted in media (NYT, S&P Global). CivAI site blocked automated fetches this session, so no CivAI contact verified; it has a press section (civai.org/press). LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/llucash (per search result, not independently verified).

name: Fabrice Berro
current_role: Co-founder of Ynsect (former Director-Data); no current position found
profile: Ensimag-trained engineer who co-founded Ynsect in 2011 with Antoine Hubert, Jean-Gabriel Levon and Alexis Angot. The French company farmed mealworm beetles for insect protein and fertilizer, raised about EUR 600M and became a unicorn, but entered judicial reorganization in March 2025 and was liquidated by the Evry commercial court on 1 Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Ynsect launched Ynfabre, described as the first industrial genomic-selection program applied to large-scale insect farming (beetle genetics), and broke ground on a giant vertical insect farm near Amiens.
deep_cut_fact: Ynsect's four founders were described as scientists and environmental activists; Berro was the Ensimag engineering graduate among them, and held the company's data role.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews, social accounts or contacts found. Ynsect was liquidated Dec 2025, so company channels no longer exist; MarketScreener/Zonebourse show no current position. Sensitive topic: avoid leading with Ynsect's collapse.

name: Nicolas Cohen
current_role: Co-founder of Ankorstore (co-CEO since 2019; current title not confirmed for 2025-26)
profile: French e-commerce entrepreneur who co-founded ALittleMarket, a leading French handmade-goods marketplace sold to Etsy in 2014, then worked at Etsy before co-founding Paris-based B2B wholesale marketplace Ankorstore in 2019. Ankorstore became a unicorn in Jan 2022 with a EUR 250M Series C (BOND, Tiger Global) at a EUR 1.75B valuation.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore hit unicorn status only about two years after launch, by which time it connected 200,000 independent retailers with 15,000 brands; Cohen said the mission was 'to swing the balance in favor of independents.'
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Ankorstore came from conversations, while he and Nicolas d'Audiffret were at Etsy after it bought their ALittleMarket, about how hard it was for Etsy sellers to grow from B2C storefronts into wholesale businesses.
notes: Common name - be careful with disambiguation. Aggregator profiles conflict on whether he is still co-CEO (one says 2019-2024). No published press email found for Ankorstore this session.
